arguments.premise_synthesis: Retail investors bought heavily during the bear market and recovery while institutions sold; Goldman Sachs US equity sentiment indicator shows significant negative territory despite all-time highs; institutional investor positioning remains light according to Goldman Sachs; and wealth advisor platforms have derisked since April and not returned to normal equity exposure, as per Chris Sadial. These factors collectively indicate that institutional under-allocation is a bullish signal, contrasting with the euphoria and amateur speculation that historically precede crashes.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The current absence of euphoria and institutional under-allocation, as evidenced by negative sentiment and light institutional positioning, establish that pre-crash indicators are not present, thus supporting the conclusion that a major crash is not imminent and disciplined long-term investing is advisable.
